title: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Sep 2026 data)
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos), fetched direct 2026-09-15 by this event's own pulse check with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,238 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup: the table headed `2026 release dates`, column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)`, row `September | Monday, September 28`. Corroborated a second time inside the primary itself — the August report at dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos/2026/2608 (HTTP 200, 62,135 bytes) states `Next release: Monday, September 28`. 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET, matching the three secondaries the 2026-09-01 entry rested on (fxstreet, tradingeconomics, investing.com). SUPERSEDES the prior `NEWS:` sourcing, which recorded dallasfed.org as HTTP 403 and not fetchable — that block was a plain-fetcher artifact and does not reproduce with browser headers. The date is now primary-verified and is NOT in doubt; it stays `estimate` on one ground only, a schema gap: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines `FED:` as `federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar` and carries no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule, so no honest confirmed prefix exists for this source. 19 of the 20 Reserve-Bank-published entries in this calendar sit at `estimate` for the same reason, and the single exception used `FED:` for a clevelandfed.org page — an inconsistency the gap produced. Filed as bottleneck #3117 by this lane on 2026-09-15, sibling to #2552 (exchange holidays) and #3058 (court dockets). Checked 2026-09-15
notes: The second regional manufacturing analog to the national ISM print, and it exists to remove a selection bias this calendar had just created. `chicago-pmi-2026-09-30` was added on 2026-08-29 because its Aug-data reading collapsed to 47.1 — the bearish regional surprise. Two days later the Dallas survey printed the opposite: general business activity 11.6 from 1.3 (highest since Jan 2025), production 16.1 from 10.1, new orders 22.0 from 6.4, with prices paid still rising. Tracking only the analog that missed low would leave the calendar structurally primed to see soft manufacturing signals and not firm ones. Filed `low`, not `medium` like Chicago: Dallas is a single-state survey that leads the national print by a full month rather than by two business days, so it is context, not a leading indicator of the next ISM. The owning ledger has since MEASURED that refusal rather than asserting it — across 20 releases the 10:30-11:30 ET hour ranks at the 52.5th (SPY) / 55.5th (QQQ) percentile of that same hour's own two-year distribution, against a null of 50. Discovered during the ism-manufacturing-2026-09-01 pulse-check adjacency sweep. WINDOW ARITHMETIC, VALIDATED AGAINST THE PRIMARY 2026-09-15: the August report states `Data were collected August 18-26`, exactly matching the release-minus-13 / release-minus-5 rule the ledger derived from the July example — so September's collection window is Sep 15-23, opening the day before the 09-16 FOMC. That window, not the headline, is why this row is read.
